blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: ___ (кот) было одиннадцать лет, и он уже не соизволил играть в мячики.
exercises.prompt: The cat was eleven years old and no longer deigned to play with balls.
exercises.why: The logical subject, that is the person who has to do something, is in the dative case: *Надо идти в класс.* The logical subject, when used with можно or нельзя, is in the dative case: *Вам можно курить, а мне нельзя. Отцу нельзя пить вино, а брату можно.* The person who needs something (or someone) is in the dative case. — From the DLI Grammar Reference Book. Lessons 35, 36, 41, 66.  ·  «The person who needs something (or someone) is in the dative case … The logical subject, when used with можно or нельзя, is in the dative case.» «This verb (нравиться) is used with the agent in the Dative case and the object (of the liking) in the Nominative case.» — DLI, Lessons 35, 36, 66.

exercises.why: The genitive case is used to denote an indefinite quantity of something: *Дайте воды, молока, хлеба.* Several masculine nouns may take the ending -у, -ю (instead of -а, -я) in the genitive case when a quantity is expressed: *Дайте, пожалуйста, супу, сахару, чаю. The genitive case of Russian nouns is more frequently used and has many more functions than any other case in the Russian language. a) The genitive case is used to denote the possessor or owner which in English is rendered by the ending -'s (-s') or by the construction with the preposition of: *Книга студента.* — The student's book.* — DLI, Lessons 23, 24, 27 and 33.  ·  «The person who needs something (or someone) is in the dative case … The logical subject, when used with можно or нельзя, is in the dative case.» «This verb (нравиться) is used with the agent in the Dative case and the object (of the liking) in the Nominative case.» — DLI, Lessons 35, 36, 66.
